mechanism.validity_test: line 710: fault iff not(pte & PTE_V) or not(pte & PTE_W) or (USER and not(pte & PTE_U)) -- i.e. the LOW BYTE only
mechanism.pt_base: line 696: pt_base = memory[PAGE_TABLE_ADDR >> 2]; pte_idx = pt_base + ((vaddr >> 8) & 0xFF); pt_base = 1536 here
mechanism.growth: lines 740-743: paddr = pfn * PAGE_WORDS + offset (pfn = pte >> 8, PAGE_WORDS = 256); if paddr >= len(memory): memory.extend([0] * (paddr + PAGE_WORDS - len(memory)))
mechanism.accepted_garbage: RAM words 1538/1539 belong to the PT window and carry byte-run data whose low byte is 0x07; the walker cannot tell them from PTEs, and there is NO bound on pfn (24-bit field -> up to ~4.3e9 words).
mechanism.existing_mitigation_that_does_not_cover_: lines 632-636 document the hazard ('bake-time text garbage under the PT window') and mitigate it by RAM-before-image ORDERING only; ordering does not help when the garbage is itself in RAM and passes the flag test.

scope: one arc consumer uses this mode: tests/test_gh18_syscall_abi.py:403 (test_gh18_syscall_table_window_reserved). Not claimed for baseline/admit (0.13-0.14 MB receipts) or for the production path.
consequences: leg A's whole-run pytest VmHWM 2684.3 MB and the file's isolated 2652.9 MB are this test's two stores (base 231 + 1078 + 1189 MB ~= 2.50 GB)

the 4 GiB worker-scope pressure behind .builder_queue/REPAIR_PENDING_worker_cgroup_memory_limit.md and .builder_queue/REPAIR_PENDING_suite_iso2_memory_containment.md is caused by this mode, so those tickets may be dissolved rather than configured around
